subject: Post-demo: Finlytics integration handoff + schema/validation questions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Finlytics integration handoff + schema/validation questions

Hi Olivia — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for your eng and procurement teams.

Summary of what Finlytics wants:
- Real-time re-ranking on query surface (embeddings + lightweight reranker).
- Deterministic structured outputs for certain downstream flows (account updates, compliance flags).
- Low-latency paths for UI (P95 <= 150ms for short prompts) and batch re-ranks overnight.

Open architecture/implementation items we discussed:
1) SDK + auth: Which SDK will you use? We can support our JS SDK for browser (with token routing) or server-side Python for private deployments. We need to confirm whether you plan to route through your backend (preferred for secrets) or want a proxy token approach.
2) Routing & fallbacks: We'll recommend a primary low-latency model + fallback to a cheaper quantized variant during peak. Need to confirm SLO tradeoffs.
3) Structured output reliability: You're asking for a constrained JSON schema for outputs and clear retry/validation behavior on decode failures. We sketched two options during the call: (A) constrained decoding + server-side validation + soft-fallback to best-effort text, (B) strict fail-fast with a re-try/backoff plan and audit logging.

Proposed immediate next steps (action owners in parentheses):
- Finlytics picks SDK & routing approach (Olivia / eng-team) — due: Tue 2027-04-05
- Redwood to produce an SDK checklist + schema example + routing diagram (Karthik / Laura) — due: Mon 2027-04-04
- Technical sync if you want to deep-dive validation/retry (Dev to lead) — propose Apr 6 or 7

Attachments: redwood-sdk-checklist.pdf (checklist for auth, streaming, token rotation), schema-proposal-v1.json (example constrained schema).

If this looks right I will drop a short tech ticket for Dev and schedule the sync.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Finlytics integration handoff + schema/validation questions

Thanks — summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SDK/auth: We will route calls via our backend (Python) so keys stay server-side. Our infra team prefers the server-side Python SDK.
- Routing: We want hard latency SLOs for UI flows (failover to cached last-good response rather than a slow fallback model). For batch re-rank jobs, we can use the cheaper quantized variant.
- Structured output: We need deterministic JSON for the compliance flags (schema required) and a tight retry policy for generation failures. Prefer \"strict fail-fast\" for compliance-critical paths; non-critical flows can be best-effort.

Would appreciate if Redwood can: (1) provide a recommended JSON schema pattern and a short validation + retry strategy (2 pages max), and (2) draft a short canary plan for the UI path so our SREs can review.

Folks on our eng team — open to a 30m sync on Apr 6 at 10am ET.

—Olivia
Head of Product | Finlytics

Adding a few technical specifics for the RFC we'll send Monday. Posting here so Olivia's eng team can see the thinking.

Key proposals (short):
- Constrained decoding: use a combination of token biasing + output-format prompt wrapper. For JSON we recommend a two-step flow for critical paths: 1) structured-only generation with a strict schema; 2) if validation fails, automatic single retry with a different sampling seed and adjusted temperature 0.0 -> 0.2.
- Validation: server-side JSON schema validation (AJV for Node / jsonschema for Python) running in the request path. Validation failures are recorded in the trace and an event emitted to Redwood's quality-monitoring.
- Retry patterns: \"single soft retry\" for UI-critical flows (low-latency budget) — attempt one quick retry with seed+tweak; if still invalid, fall back to cached last-good or an explicit client-visible error with a trace id. For batch jobs, allow up to 3 retries with exponential backoff and a review queue for persistent mismatches.
- Observability: include schema version and prompt-id in traces; count and alert on parse-fail rate > 0.5% for compliance flows.

Deliverables Monday (Laura / Dev):
- schema-proposal-v1.json (attached)
- lightweight canary plan doc (link to Drive)
- SDK checklist with sample auth header examples

Thanks all — quick technical plan and proposed meeting agenda for the Apr 6 sync: please confirm availability. I tried to keep the agenda practical and time-boxed.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: Quick intro + target success criteria (Olivia/Karthik)
- 10m: SDK & auth pattern (Dev) — token rotation, audience-restricted tokens, and proxy routing examples (Python snippet)
- 8m: Structured output reliability (Laura) — constrained decoding options, schema validation, retry budget and fallback behaviors
- 5m: Next-step checklist & owners (Karthik)

Implementation notes:
- Python SDK snippet (proxy routing):
  - Use server-side SDK with short-lived session tokens. Example header: Authorization: Bearer r_infer_session_XXXX (rotate every 1h).
  - For browser telemetry, use a lightly permissioned client token that only allows streaming & metrics, not generation.
- Constrained decoding + validation flow (pseudo):
  1) Request with prompt wrapper that asks strictly for JSON and passes schema id.
  2) On server, run schema validator. If pass -> return to UI.
  3) If fail -> perform single retry with deterministic seed change and temperature 0.0 -> 0.15.
  4) If still fail -> mark event, return last-good cached response or explicit parse-fail signal with trace_id.
- Reranker/embeddings: will recommend a hybrid approach — embeddings for candidate generation + small-classifier reranker for final ordering. We'll include the sample re-rank latency numbers in the doc.

I attached the SDK checklist and the initial schema proposal. I'll produce a 2-page validation & retry strategy doc before the sync and share the Drive link here.

Next actionable items (short):
- Olivia: confirm Apr 6 10am ET or propose alternate
- Finlytics Eng: decide whether to use client-side telemetry tokens or entirely server-side routing
- Redwood: deliver 2-page validation/retry doc + canary plan by Apr 5 EOD
